_comment: Every colour, timing and size knob in the UI lives here. Nothing visual is hard-coded in a component. Edit this file, reload, done.

unit._comment: Colloquial unit cards cycle through these; a unit's number picks one, so the same unit keeps its colour.

tab._comment: default is what an unknown id wears, the primary purple, so colorFor('tab', id) is the one rule for tab colour everywhere.

science._comment: Card colour of each map science (ui/MapPanel), keyed by chart id. One hue each, all readable on the raised surface, borrowed from the tab palette.

space._comment: Gaps shared across tabs. panel is the gap between the blocks of every tab, header included (the .panel class).

layer._comment: The one stacking scale: every z-index in the app is one of these, never a bare number. Lowest first: raised lifts a piece over its neighbours, seal is the Quran backdrop, below the page so results sit over it, backdrop is the drifting-lights canvas, below even the seal, sticky is a bar that pins while scrolling, popover a floating panel opened from a button, header the app bar, overlay a full-screen sheet, tip a tooltip over everything.

backdrop._comment: The faint seal behind a tab (ui/QuranSeal). ink is its colour, strength how much of it shows (wide: once a search fills the page); a light theme changes these two only.

lights._comment: The lantern backdrop: soft out-of-focus lights drifting slowly on a dark warm ground, behind every tab. count is how many lights, size-min-px and size-max-px how wide the smallest and largest are, speed how far one drifts per frame at motion.scale 1 (so the Animations setting slows it, and 0 stops it), alpha how bright a light is at its middle. tint is the share of lights that wear the tab's own colour instead of one of the warm lights, so the tab changes the room without painting it. Kept faint on purpose: the words on top are the point, and lights that compete with them are a distraction rather than a mood. ground-top and ground-bottom are the dark the lights float on. colors is the warm lights, comma separated, that the rest of the lights are drawn from.

marks._comment: Large faint Arabic letters drawn on the backdrop canvas under the lights, in the tab's colour, so the page reads as Arabic before a word is on it. count is how many (0 draws none), size-min-rem and size-max-rem the range of letter heights, alpha how visible each is (kept far below the lights so the words on the glass stay the point), drift-px how far a letter wanders from where it sits (0 holds it still; speed is the backdrop's, so the Animations setting slows it), letters the pool drawn from, repeats welcome, and font the face, which must be the one the app already loads for Arabic.

glass._comment: The frosted pane the page content sits on, so the lights behind it read as a soft glow rather than as noise under the words. blur-px is how far the lights are smeared, alpha how much of the surface colour covers them (100% would hide them).

tabstrip._comment: How much of its own colour an unselected tab keeps. 0% is plain grey, 100% is as loud as the selected one.

timeline._comment: The timelines tab: acc-s and acc-l are the saturation and lightness every section hue is drawn at (its accent), ink-l the lightness of text in that hue; then the map's two grounds. Every section wears the tab's own colour, so the Seerah and the unseen sections read as one design.

cursor-light._comment: The cursor light: one faint circle that follows the pointer on every tab, tinted by the tab's own colour, so the page points at what is being read without a word of instruction. size-px is how wide it reaches, white how much white sits in the middle, and tint how much of the tab's colour bleeds out from it. Small and faint on purpose: at full strength it reads as a torch and the text under it stops being the point. The Animations setting turns it off with everything else.

tamreen._comment: The two underline colours on a Tamreen picture question: blue for a possible حال, green for a possible ذو الحال. Their own group, not 'role', because they mark a candidate in the picture rather than a settled grammatical role.

mic._comment: The capsule microphone, the mark that means dictation: capsule, three grille slits, cradle arc, stem. weight is the stroke on the mark's own 24-grid, so it scales with wherever it is drawn. pulse-ms is one beat of the grille level-meter while recording; hover-pulse-ms is that same beat run slowly on hover, a preview of what pressing does. chase-ms is one lap of the arc's chasing dash while thinking.

lexicon._comment: The shelf of classical dictionaries under a root. entry-h is how much of an entry is shown before the rest is folded behind Show all: Taj al-Arus on أمر is 23,000 letters, and printed whole one book would bury the three under it. Enough to tell whether this is the entry wanted, not enough to be a wall. In rem, so a browser's own text setting moves it with the words.

command._comment: The command line: the bar in the header and the orbit launcher behind the pen. rest-w is how wide the bar sits when nobody is using it and open-w how wide it grows on focus, both in rem, so a longer placeholder needs a number changed here and not a class edited. orbit-r is the radius the seven tabs sit at in the launcher, sat-w the width of one of them, and rail-w the strip of letters beside a result list.

wheel._comment: Every dropdown is ui/WheelPicker. type-from is how many choices a list needs before its card shows a box to type in; a shorter list is quicker to spin.

dance._comment: How a group of things arrives: each one small and gathered at the middle, then springing out to where it belongs, one after another. Written as its own group rather than inside the launcher because it is the .dance class in styles/motion.css, which anything can wear: a ring of tabs, a row of cards, a set of chips. from-scale is how small each starts, from-spread how far along its own spoke it starts as a fraction of the full distance (1 means it does not travel, only grows), and beats how many springs the whole arrival lasts. The gap between one and the next is motion.stagger-ms, shared with every other staggered thing in the app.

motion._comment: Plain numbers, so a CSS duration is built as calc(var(--motion-base-ms) * 1ms). scale is the switch for the ambient loops (the pen bobbing, the mic grille, the mic ring, the shimmer): their choreography keeps its own tempo, multiplied by this, so the Animations setting can stop them all by driving it to 0.
motion._patience_comment: Not an animation: how a wait is announced. Nothing is said for the first patience-ms, because an answer that arrives sooner than that has arrived at once as far as the eye is concerned, and a spinner shown and taken away inside a fifth of a second reads as a flash rather than as news. Once something has been said it stays for patience-hold-ms, so an answer landing just after the wait was announced does not snatch it away again. Read in JavaScript by lib/useSlowPending.js, not by the stylesheet, so the Animations setting leaves it alone.

landing._comment: The welcome page's one vertical rhythm: the top and bottom breathing room of every section (hero, manuscript band, tools, shift, finale). Fluid between 64px on a phone and 112px on a wide screen. Change it here and every section moves together.
landing._band_comment: The slim strips between big sections (the trusted-sources banner). Small on purpose, so the strip sits snug against the section above and below it instead of floating in space.
landing._gutter_comment: The side margin every landing section shares, so text and cards line up down the whole page instead of each section picking its own.
landing._tree_comment: How far the sentence-demo tree is shrunk to fit. tree-zoom-tablet is used under 1100px wide, tree-zoom-narrow under 820px, tree-zoom-phone under 600px. Below about 0.5 the labels stop being readable, so on a phone the tree keeps a readable size and the page scroll pans it sideways inside its frame instead.
landing._size_comment: Fixed sizes that used to sit in the stylesheet. strip-w and strip-h are one tool card in the scroll strip; sd-min-h is the shortest the sentence-demo frame gets; arch-max-w is the hero video frame when it stacks; edge is the gap from the pinned demo's top and bottom to its label and caption.
landing._phone_comment: Phone only. sd-phone-start is how much of the screen (in percent, a bare number) the sentence-demo card fills before the reader scrolls, so it can grow to the full screen instead of being full already. strip-w-sm and strip-aspect size a tool card in the strip on a phone: nearly the screen wide, and the same shape as the recordings (16 by 10) so the whole screen shows instead of a cropped slice.
landing._story_comment: The scroll story: four demo steps on one centred stage. story-track-h is how much scrolling the whole story takes (about a screen per step), story-col-w the width of the column, story-stage-h the stage (story-stage-h-sm on a phone). story-panel-bg is the dark glass each demo sits on, story-panel-r its corner. step-dim is how faint the steps not yet reached are in the pill row. star-size is the turning geometric star behind the stage, star-turn how far it has turned by the end, star-opacity how strong its lines are. wave-ms is one swell of the recitation waveform, wave-bars how many bars it has, cap-w the widest a caption gets.

layout._comment: How wide the page is allowed to get. Everything down the middle of the app reads this one number through the .shell class, so the header, the tab strip, the banner and the panels can never disagree about where the edges are. It is a maximum, not a width: on any screen narrower than this the page simply fills it, which is what keeps the phone view working.
layout._control_comment: One square for every small control in the page chrome: the settings gear, the pen that opens the launcher, and the height of the command bar between them. One number, so the two ends of the header can never disagree about how tall the row is.
layout._chip_comment: How tall a chip stands, whatever is written in it. Said here rather than left to the text because a pill that takes its height from its own letters is a different height in Arabic than in English: a Recent row holding both came out with the Arabic pills at exactly twice the height of the English ones, a ragged row that looked like a browser bug and was not.
layout._tap_comment: The least height a pill or link stands on a touch screen, where a finger needs more than a pointer does. styles/text.css applies it to .tap when the pointer is coarse; a mouse keeps the compact sizes.

sheet._comment: How big a pop-up may get on a wide screen. Maximums, not widths: a phone stays full width. narrow is a short list of choices (settings, a Grow step), standard a pop-up with reading in it (the chain, a phrase, the word bank), wide a pop-up laid out in columns (the sections menu). tall is how much of the screen height any of them may take. narrator is the widest a name box grows in the chain drawing before it wraps.

shadow._comment: Depth, for the few things that float over the page rather than sit in it: a tooltip, a popover. Only one so far, on purpose, one lift reads as one layer.

arabic._comment: One ladder for every piece of Arabic in the app, in rem. Four rungs, smallest first, one for each of ui/ArabicText's sizes: tiny is a name inside another name in the tarkeeb diagram; small is a term or a table cell; reading is Arabic being read: an ayah, a memorise page, a dictionary entry, the sentence a diagram is drawn under; display is a word on its own, in a search box or as an answer. The diagram used to keep a ladder of its own, and then a rung of its own, and both times its words drifted a third bigger than the same sentence in the word cards under it. Anything Arabic picks a rung here; nothing sets a size of its own.

urdu._comment: Urdu rides the Arabic ladder above; only what genuinely differs is here. Nastaliq slopes each word down to the left, so a line needs far more room under it than Naskh does, and two lines set at the Arabic height overlap. Raise this if descenders touch the line below; styles/text.css swaps it in wherever lang="ur".

hadith._comment: The words of a hadith, printed under an event in the timelines. said is what was actually said, which the books mark with quote marks; told is the telling around it, the chain of narrators and what happened between the sayings, drawn back because it is read past rather than read. lines is how much of one hadith shows before the rest waits behind Show the rest.
hadith._way_comment: The chain drawing colours the word between two narrators by how it was received: heard (سمعت، حدّثنا، أخبرنا) and loose (عن, which does not say how). The chain words guide wears the same two.

type._comment: English text sizes. In rem, so a browser's own text setting still moves them; px would ignore it. micro/tiny/small are supporting labels, badges, captions, the note under a control. body is English being read rather than labelled: an ayah's translation, a verse's gloss. A translation set at a label size is the mistake this token exists to stop, so reach for body whenever the English is the content.
type._figure_comment: A number read at a glance rather than in a sentence: the three counts on the quiz panel's shut bar. Larger than body on purpose, it is what the row exists to show and it has to win against the words beside it.
type._label_comment: The two rungs the rest of the app is written in: label is a control's own words (a chip, a select, a count) and ui is a line of English inside a control or a card. Tailwind's text-xs and text-sm are pointed at these two in styles/base.css, so every size in the app comes from this file and there is no second scale hiding in the components.
type.label: 0.75rem

_tarkeeb_comment: The diagram has no sizes of its own any more. Its sentence is the arabic 'heading' rung, its role names 'small', a name inside another name 'tiny', and its + signs the English type 'body' size. Depth still reads as size, the steps are just shared with the rest of the app instead of being a second private ladder. Its colours are the 'role' group.
